summary: This was a seven-minute run started by the service when the settle-then-step loop (E0090, Hatteras job 164664) finished. There was no instruction and nothing under Asked, so the answers list is empty. It made no claims, and no challenges were open on this line. Its numbers check out: I refetched the four steps in the gap and the Gamma 2.55 step, and every amplitude, both over the whole step and over the last hundred cycles, reproduces to the fourth decimal. The checksums match the manifest of A0173 and the evidence file. The registered test was scored correctly: (iii) is falsified as registered, with a gap of 0.111 diameters. The main problem is how the result is read. The line's state, the headline and the PROGRAM.md entry compare the new loop's settled-window gap (0.021 diameters at Gamma 2.2, 0.048 at 2.25) with the 400-cycle loop's whole-step gap (0.103). Those are two different windows, which breaks the rule that the baseline is compared the same way. I re-read the 400-cycle loop over its last hundred cycles (A0064). Its gap there is 0.039 at Gamma 2.2 and 0.069 at 2.25. Most of the drop the session reports therefore comes from changing the window, not from settling. The settle-then-step loop also gave the layer less time, not more: 7050 cycles in all against 11600, and at Gamma 2.2 on the way down exactly the same 400 cycles. So the sentence in L0017's state, 'The gap at 2.2 was the ramp being too fast', does not hold. The same goes for the summary's takeaway that 'most of the gap seen at fixed rates was the ramp being too fast'. A fair statement: read over the last hundred cycles, the gap at 2.2 is 0.02 settled against 0.04 at 400 cycles a step, and at 2.25 it is 0.05 against 0.07. Both differences are within the roughly 0.05 wandering seen on one seed. The session saw part of this itself: its second proposed direction asks to re-read the 400-cycle loop the same way. But it printed the uneven comparison as the line's state anyway. Two smaller points. The summary's 'ran the frozen tests (74 passed)' is not in any evidence file. That pytest run wrote to ~/.tmp/pytest-of-roborobo/pytest-7 at 06:13:42, inside this session's window and outside the two allowed folders. program check passes apart from my own scratch folder, which I have removed. It lists four approvals in the last day for Chris to confirm.

run_conditions.assessment: The run started at 06:11:03, two minutes before its scheduled 06:11, and committed at 06:17:09. It collected one finished two-day Hatteras job (48.14 CPU-hours, matching the job record) and analysed it, and nothing was left waiting except Chris's answer to its two questions. Nothing is running: active.jsonl is empty. Disk is fine: 91 GB free against the 40 GB floor, and sequel-data at about 0.6 GB against the 15 GB ceiling once my fetched files were removed. tmp/ was empty when the session ended. The machine did not limit the science. One seed is a limit of the registered design, not of the machine. The load average now is 4.7 on 40 cores, consistent with the recorded 30.6 cores available.
discrepancies: limits_hit says the session 'ran the frozen tests (74 passed)'. No evidence file records that run. Its only trace is a pytest temporary folder, ~/.tmp/pytest-of-roborobo/pytest-7 (06:13:42), which is outside sequel and sequel-data.
cpu_hours 48.14 is the Hatteras job's CPU over two days, recorded in this session because it was collected here. That is reasonable, but none of it was spent during the seven-minute window.
pmset is not available on this Linux machine, as the summary says, so sleep could not be checked. The commit and file times show no gap.
